messages:
support-ash: FYI we're getting a sharp spike in 503s for hosted inference (customer tenant: acme-corp) starting ~15:02 UTC. CS are getting angry. root logs show upstream worker exits + container restart loop.
oncall-lina: Can you paste the gateway request id + example timeframe? I want to pull traces.
support-ash: req=gw_6a7b2, window=15:02:12-15:06:00 UTC. P95 latency jumps then 503s. From host logs:
```
2026-03-17T15:03:10Z infer-worker[pid=2345]: signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 0, addr 0x7ff...
2026-03-17T15:03:11Z containerd: killing container infer-runner-xyz status=137
2026-03-17T15:03:12Z orchestrator: restarted infer-runner-xyz
```
eng-ryan: segfault from the worker, interesting. Any GPU OOM messages in the kernel logs or nvidia-smi?
support-ash: There's a rapid sequence of prefetch/kvcache allocations just before the crash, and dmesg shows cuda OOM-ish resets on the same host. Not a clear full OOM but card reset.
sre-kofi: tagging in. I pulled the node metrics: GPU memory at crash ~98% for that process, big host-level mem growth too. This was during a large multipart request set (several parallel toolcalls) from acme's tenant.
eng-ryan: Which model + runtime config? Could be quant swap + large context causing unexpected allocation pattern.
support-ash: model=redwood-v1-13b-quant, runtime=rv-infer-2.1, env var KV_PREFETCH=enabled, dynbatch=on.
ops-bot: deploy bot: new build rv-infer-2.1.3 rolled to pool-07 at 2026-03-17T14:58:00Z (hash abc123).
oncall-lina: That timeframe matches the deploy. Possible regression in 2.1.3 + kv-prefetch + large multi-part payloads.
eng-ryan: Repro steps I ran locally: small script that parallelizes 6 multipart uploads (each ~120k tokens metadata) to that model which triggers high KV prefetch and ballooning. I got a single segfault locally in a container with quant kernels. Sending gdb backtrace to thread.
support-ash: paste gdb bt here please.
eng-ryan: ```
#0  0x00007f9a2b1a in attention_kernel::compute(...)
#1  0x00007f9a2c2b in kv_prefetch::prefetch_batch(...)
#2  0x000055a1c3d0 in runner::handle_request(...)
#3  0x000055a1c3e5 in main_loop
```
sre-kofi: Looks like attention kernel touched an invalid pointer after a prefetch path. Could be race between eviction and prefetch.
eng-ryan: Quick mitigation: disable KV_PREFETCH on the hosted pool for quant models and pin acme-corp to pools with 2.1.2 until we patch. That should avoid the prefetch codepath.
cs-jamie: I'm drafting a CS message. Do we have an ETA for a hotfix?
oncall-lina: Immediate mitigation steps I'm doing now: 1) disable KV_PREFETCH for pool-07 2) scale pool-07 to reduce co-tenancy for acme 3) rollback rv-infer to 2.1.2 on that pool. I'll monitor 10m.
ops-bot: orchestrator: applied config change KV_PREFETCH=false to pool-07 (rolled to 5/7 nodes)
sre-kofi: After disabling prefetch the error rate dropped ~80% in the next 5m and no new segfaults. Good sign.
eng-ryan: Root cause hypothesis: regressed prefetch path in 2.1.3 that can dereference freed memory under high multipart/parallel requests for quant kernels. Repro confirmed locally with stress script.
support-ash: Notes for postmortem: timeline, deploy correlation, reproducer script, gdb bt, node GPU memory graphs, and mitigation steps (disable prefetch, rollback). Also include customer impact and CS copy.
cs-jamie: I'll notify acme-corp with a short update: we've mitigated and are rolling a targeted fix, will follow up with RCA.
eng-ryan: Action items: 1) eng to prepare 2.1.4 patch that guards prefetch pointer lifetime + add unit test (owner: ryan) 2) SRE to run increased soak on 2.1.4 in canary (owner: kofi) 3) Support/CS to update affected customers (owner: jamie).
sre-kofi: I'll open an escalation ticket with priority P1 and attach logs + the local reproducer.
ops-bot: incident-tracker: created INC-2026-0317-042 with severity=P1, assignees=[eng-ryan,sre-kofi,cs-jamie].
support-ash: Closing loop for now — monitoring continues, 503 rate is back to baseline for acme. Will update thread if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
